WoW: Forever

Feral — Bear Druid

Leather tanking in Bear Form on rage and dodge: no block, no parry. This is your only combat form between levels 10 and 20, so every Druid plays it whether they intend to tank or not.

WoW: Forever · Tank · Updated October 5, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70124 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Bear build has been tested. Bear and Cat share one talent tree and mostly one build. They have separate pages here because the rotations, stat priorities and gear are completely different even where the talents are not. No source has posted a level 30 build either — the cap only reached 30 on October 1 and none of the three has published one since — so the level 30 line below extends the published level 20 build using the full talent tree's point costs, not a build any guide has recommended. Blizzard's own caveat: "class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes."

What Bear is for

Taking hits in leather: Bear Form multiplies the armour on your gear, adds +180 health, and you can drop form and heal yourself with Mana. Growl on an 8-second cooldown holds what you pull, rage comes from being hit as well as hitting, and in Forever the weapon's damage counts in Bear Form, so more damage means more threat.

You do not get a choice before level 20. Bear Form comes from a class quest at 10; Cat Form does not exist until 20. The published advice: "As you reach Level 10 you will mainly want to level in Bear Form, using your Mana to heal yourself after killing enemies, and then recovering your Mana while in Bear Form."

Be aware the class starts slowly: "Since Bear Form is not unlocked until Level 10, and Cat Form first at level 20, Feral Druid has a fairly slow start."

Three tanks — Protection Warrior, Protection Paladin and Feral Druid — is the common assumption, not a Blizzard taxonomy: Blizzard's own Druid deep dive credits Druids with the "ability to serve any combat role" and publishes no tank list.

Your talent points

Level 20: 0/11/0. Four different level-20 Feral builds are published and they disagree on most of the eleven points. Here is the one with a published click order:

  1. Ferocity, 5 points: "helping with both your Rage economy while leveling allowing for more Maul casts, and reducing your energy cost in Cat Form"
  2. Brutal Impact, 2 points: "both strengthen your Bash and reduces the cooldown by 30 seconds"
  3. Feral Instinct, 1 point: "for Swipe damage and improved Prowl at Level 20." Blizzard's class deep dive confirms the mechanism: it no longer increases threat in Bear Form; instead it increases Swipe's damage. The stealth (Prowl) bonuses are unchanged
  4. Feral Swiftness, 2 points: "a sizable movement speed increase in Cat Form, and an added benefit of granting increased Dodge chance in all forms." Blizzard's class deep dive confirms both halves directly and adds a row move: moved from row 3 to row 2, the Cat Form speed bonus now works indoors, and the Dodge bonus applies all the time, not only in Cat Form
  5. Feral Charge at 20 — the 11-point gold medal talent. Per Blizzard, it now also grants a Cat Form version, on a 30-second cooldown that does not interrupt or immobilize the target

A tank-specific alternative skips Ferocity entirely for armour: Heart of the Wild 5 / Feral Swiftness 2 / Thick Hide 3 / Feral Charge 1.

A third: Ferocity 5 / Heart of the Wild 3 / Feral Swiftness 2 / Feral Charge 1. "The fastest way to go — literally, due to Feral Swiftness and Feral Charge."

Level 30: 0/21/0 — our own extension, not a published build. No source has posted one. A dual-role reading adds Savage Fury 2 · Sharpened Claws 2 · Predatory Strikes 3 · Blood Frenzy 2 · Leader of the Pack 1. A tank-specific reading takes Feral Instinct 3 and Primal Bite 1 instead of the cat mobility. Both spend the twenty-first point on Leader of the Pack.

Threat and mitigation rotation

  1. Growl to pull and to hold. Rage comes from taking hits and auto-attacking
  2. Enrage: 30 rage over 10 seconds on a 1-minute cooldown, "at the cost of reducing your Armor slightly"
  3. Faerie Fire to strip armour. In Forever this is usable in Bear, Dire Bear or Cat Form, which it was not in Classic — per Blizzard it costs no resources but gains a 6-second cooldown, and as of October 1 it no longer resets your swing timer when used. Known bug, not intended design: Blizzard's October 1 Known Issues list states multiple debuffs, Faerie Fire named specifically, currently generate no threat — do not rely on it to help hold aggro until that is fixed
  4. Maul as your rage dump
  5. Bash to stun, and with Brutal Impact it comes back much faster

Pre-buff Mark of the Wild and Thorns. Drop form to self-heal. Nature's Grasp or Entangling Roots to disengage. Both now work in form and indoors.

Multi-target: Swipe, and know its limit. Swipe hits three targets. The published warning: "Three-target Primal Bite does not secure a fourth or fifth enemy on its own, and Swipe also only strikes three nearby enemies." Note Primal Bite only hits three under Berserk, a level-40 capstone. Below that it is single-target, so Swipe's three is your whole answer. As of October 1, Swipe correctly scales with Attack Power, gaining 3% of your attack power — it was bugged and did not before. Blizzard says the in-game tooltip will not reflect this until a future update, so what the ability's own text shows you is wrong in the meantime.

Stat priority

Stamina and armour first, then Agility (dodge and more armour), then Defense.

Bear Form multiplies the armour on your gear, so a leather piece with a high armour number beats the same stats on cloth. And the Forever-specific part: the weapon's damage counts in Bear Form, and more damage means more threat, so choose the weapon on its stats and its damage together. Blizzard's own description of the mechanism: auto-attack DPS in Bear, Cat or Dire Bear Form now equals your weapon's DPS outright, at a fixed 2.5-second swing speed in Bear/Dire Bear (1.0 second in Cat Form), and weapon-damage abilities use the same numbers.

One published tank list orders it Defense > Dodge > Armor > Agility > Strength > Attack Power > crit > Haste. One source disputes the weapon-damage priority outright, arguing you should "Compare the item's form-relevant bonuses, armor, Stamina and defense instead of importing a Warrior list." Three sources and the client data are on the other side, but the disagreement is real.

Your kit, by level

The Forever Feral spellbook is thin under the cap.

LevelWhat you get
10Class quest. Bear Form, Growl, Maul, Demoralizing Roar
12Enrage
14Bash
16Swipe, your only area attack
28Cower, Challenging Roar
30Travel Form
36Frenzied Regeneration
40Dire Bear Form
42Lacerate

So a level-30 bear has no Lacerate, no Dire Bear Form and no Frenzied Regeneration. That is most of the tanking kit, and it is why no beta report tells you much about tanking. Per Blizzard, Lacerate at 42 applies a Bleed over 15 seconds stacking up to 5 times, and reapplying it against an existing stack deals 10% weapon damage per stack on top — a high-threat bleed, not merely a DoT.

What defines Bear

TalentEarliest levelWhat it does
Thick Hide 3/317Completely rewritten, and compressed from five ranks to three. Classic gave +10% armour from items at 5/5; Forever gives +3 base armour per level and +2 more per point of defense skill above five times your level, multiplied by your form. It also applies in Cat, Dire Bear and Moonkin Form, not just Bear
Primal Bite~25The new single-target rage button: 100% weapon damage plus 26, for 20 Rage on a 6-second cooldown, usable only in Bear or Dire Bear Form. Requires Savage Fury as a prerequisite. This is the talent formerly called Mangle — Blizzard's own words: "We have opted to go with this ability instead of Mangle" — and the rename is finished in the client: "All talents referencing Mangle now reference Primal Bite." Mangle is gone from the spellbook. Its threat generation was roughly doubled in the October 1 build — our own reading of that change, which no source has published, is to prioritise it over Maul once you have it
Natural Reaction39New, Bear-oriented, row 6. It increases your Dodge chance and gives each Dodge a chance to grant 5 rage — Blizzard publishes neither a rank count nor the percentages
Berserk40The 31-point capstone — 15-second duration, 3-minute cooldown, usable in Bear, Cat or Dire Bear Form. Not in the beta

What Forever changed for Bear

  • Thick Hide is a different talent under the same name (above): base armour per level and defense scaling, rather than a percentage of your gear.
  • Frenzied Regeneration is now a real defensive cooldown: "Each point of Rage is converted into 1% health", where Classic gave 10 flat health. Ranks 2 and 3 were deleted; the one remaining rank trains at 36.
  • Enrage front-loads: "Instantly generates 10 Rage and another 20 Rage over 10 sec", where Classic gave 20 over 10 with nothing up front.
  • Bear Form and Dire Bear Form now generate 75% increased Rage on a critical strike (October 1) — another reason crit gear is not purely wasted on a tank.
  • All Shapeshift Forms are now immune to Disarm (October 1). The nuance matters for a tank: if you are disarmed before you shift, the form does not clear the Disarm, and you deal reduced damage for its duration — so a mob or boss that disarms you before you can shift still works.
  • Bear Form's health bonus went from +20 to +180. Growl's cooldown dropped to 8 seconds. Demoralizing Roar is −46 attack power, up from −30. Faerie Fire is usable in Bear, Dire Bear and Cat Form.
  • A new rage economy: Natural Reaction gives a chance of rage on dodge, Blood Frenzy gives it on crit. Improved Enrage and Faerie Fire (Feral) are gone as talents because their effects became baseline: Enrage now front-loads 10 rage itself, and ordinary Faerie Fire works in form. Lacerate was added.
  • Heart of the Wild kept its bear clause exactly: +20% Stamina at 5/5, the same as Classic, while the Intellect and Cat Strength clauses were both halved to +10%. It also moved from tier 6 to tier 1, which is why a level-20 build can take it.
  • One rename, and one merge — both confirmed directly by Blizzard's class deep dive. Mangle is now Primal Bite (and lost its debuff): "We have opted to go with this ability instead of Mangle." Separately, Classic's Primal Fury (the Bear rage talent) and Blood Frenzy (the Cat combo-point talent) were merged into one node, and Blizzard's own text is explicit that the merged node is called Blood Frenzy: "The effects of the old Primal Fury and Blood Frenzy talent have been combined into this single 2-point talent." It carries the Bear rage clause plus a Cat clause Classic did not have. Primal Fury is not selectable in the Forever tree, so build lists naming it cannot be entered as printed; ClassicWoW.gg has the direction the other way round. Half the guide sites still use the old Mangle name for the renamed node.

At level 60

Unknown. Whether Bear holds threat and survives without Classic's armour-from-items scaling is untested. Nobody has had Berserk, Lacerate, Dire Bear Form, Frenzied Regeneration or a level-60 defense value.

Sources

Compiled from the three major Forever guide sites and cross-checked against each other. Where Blizzard has published an official class deep dive, that post outranks all three and the page is written from it. Everything else — talent ranks, tooltip values, what exists in the tree at all — is settled against the client itself, read through foreverchanges.pro and wago.tools. Where the guides disagree with each other, this page says which said what.
